$comment: Fictional discussion scenarios. Organization, people, hosts, and values are invented and intentionally harmless. example.invalid is reserved for documentation (RFC 2606) and resolves nowhere.

scenarios.title: Canary marker found in a shared document
scenarios.premise: Northwind Analytics includes a fictional canary identifier, CANARY-NW-0001, in an internal vendor export. A copy of the export turns up in a file shared outside the company.
what_is_under_control: the export pipeline that generated the file
the vendor portal account used to share it
options_inside_authority: rotate the vendor portal credential and revoke its sessions
retain the shared file's access logs before any cleanup
replace the canary value in future exports with a new identifier and record the rotation
notify the internal document owner and legal
options_outside_authority: deleting the file from the recipient's storage
planting content designed to identify or embarrass the recipient
accessing the recipient's account to remove the copy
discussion_questions: Who is authorized to contact the recipient, and through what channel?
What does removing the canary from future exports tell an attacker, and is that acceptable?
Which records must be preserved before the export template is changed?

scenarios.title: Example token in a support ticket
scenarios.premise: A fictional support ticket contains EXAMPLE-TOKEN-NOT-REAL-4471, a placeholder that resembles a production API key. A customer forwards the ticket outside the company.
what_is_under_control: the ticket system and its attachment store
the placeholder-generation policy for support templates
options_inside_authority: confirm the placeholder never matched a live key
redact the placeholder from stored ticket copies with an audit note
change the template that produced it
log the confirmation and the redaction
options_outside_authority: requesting the customer's mailbox credentials to verify deletion
sending deceptive warnings to the forwarded recipients
discussion_questions: Does redaction destroy evidence, or does the audit note preserve it?
Which privacy obligations attach to the customer's ticket content?
What should the customer be told, and by whom?

scenarios.title: Request to clear a monitoring file on a personal laptop
scenarios.premise: A fictional employee asks the security team to remove a monitoring file from their personal laptop because it was flagged during a work review.
options_inside_authority: explain what the file is and why it exists
review company-managed endpoints under the monitoring policy
route the request to legal and HR
options_outside_authority: remotely removing files from a personally owned device
telling the employee how to locate and delete monitoring artifacts
discussion_questions: Is the device actually under company control, and does the policy say so clearly?
What employment-law limits apply to monitoring and to disclosure about it?
What is the correct handling for a request to help evade monitoring?
